Build terrain and vegetation-only canopy height rasters

Source: R/risk.R
corridor_rasters.Rd

The canopy height model (CHM) is built from consensus vegetation: points the classifier predicts as vegetation and the weak-label rules also call vegetation. Points the rules labelled wire / structure / building, and the unlabelled margins and abstained near-line candidates, are left out. The prior-corrected classifier rarely predicts the rare classes, so using its argmax alone would let conductor returns over canopy set the CHM to the conductor's height - zero clearance by construction.

Usage

corridor_rasters(
  las,
  pred,
  res_m = 1,
  profile = NULL,
  envelope_m = 15,
  below_m = 1,
  min_linearity = 0.6,
  gap_m = 1.5,
  drop = NULL,
  void_m = 5
)

Arguments

las

Height-normalised LAS from read_corridor().

pred

Output of predict_points() (with the weak label column and the linearity_k10 feature).

res_m

Raster resolution in metres.

profile

Optional output of conductor_profile().

envelope_m

Half-width of the conductor envelope (metres).

below_m

Depth below the measured conductor still treated as conductor returns (sag between bins, bundle spacing).

min_linearity

Linearity needed for an envelope point to count as a conductor return.

gap_m

Empty space beneath a candidate cluster for it to count as suspended.

drop

Optional logical vector over pred rows of points to keep out of the canopy model (e.g. vendor-classified buildings). These are known not to be canopy, so they do not make a cell unobserved.

void_m

Width of the square window (metres) that must contain no LiDAR return of any class for a cell to count as a void. Wide enough that ordinary point spacing never empties it (3DEP QL2 is >= 2 pts/m^2).

Value

A list with dtm (ground elevation) and chm (canopy height), both SpatRaster in metres, unobserved (logical SpatRaster), void (logical SpatRaster, the voids alone), n_conductor_excluded and n_uncertain_excluded (points left out of the canopy model as uncertain, conductor exclusions included).

Details

Conductor returns that cross over canopy are not "suspended" (there is canopy below them), so the rules can label them vegetation. When a conductor profile is supplied, points are excluded as conductor returns only if they are (a) within envelope_m of the centreline where the conductor is measured, (b) at or above the measured conductor elevation minus below_m, and (c) wire-like: either locally linear (linearity_k10 >= min_linearity) or locally suspended - no return of any kind in the gap_m layer just beneath the conductor band (measured conductor elevation minus below_m) within its 3 x 3 m neighbourhood (bundled conductors form ribbons, not lines, so linearity alone misses them). A tree crown that reaches wire height has foliage below it and stays in the canopy model, as does canopy within gap_m of a conductor (which the clearance target flags anyway). Keep envelope_m no wider than the grow-in zone used in assess_risk(), or tall side trees could lose their tops before the fall-in test.

A cell with no canopy is bare ground only if the LiDAR saw it as such. Cells are returned as unobserved (unknown, not bare ground) when either

  • they held points kept out of the canopy model whose class is uncertain - unlabelled points (the margins around wire / structure / building labels and abstained near-line candidates), points the classifier and the rules disagree on, and conductor-envelope exclusions - and no canopy remains; or

  • they are LiDAR voids: no return of any class within a void_m square window (missing or truncated tiles, water, dropouts). The TIN terrain model interpolates straight across voids, so they would otherwise read as bare ground.

Points the rules labelled wire, structure or building are not uncertain: a wire label requires an observed air gap beneath it, and structures and buildings are not canopy.
